## The shared layer

Backend modules import the shared types, such as `Chat`, `ChatOpts` and
`Resp`, from `urai` directly. The tests below check that importing
`rishi.core` registers the runtimes and does not copy Urai’s namespace.

[`RishiToolLoop`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rishi/core.html#rishitoolloop)
is the base class for the backends that drive Urai’s tool loop. These
are llama.cpp, MLX, Ollama, the hosted API and Claude Code. Copilot uses
it through the hosted API class. LiteRT-LM does not use it, because the
LiteRT-LM engine runs tools itself.
[`RishiToolLoop`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rishi/core.html#rishitoolloop)
turns on three callbacks by default. `UsageCallback` counts token usage.
`ToolReminderCallback` reminds the model which tools it has.
`SlidingWindowCallback` removes old messages when the context window is
full.

[`split_model_path`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rishi/core.html#split_model_path)
turns a model name into a Hugging Face repo id or a local file path. It
removes any runtime prefix first. An explicit `model_path` argument
takes priority over a path in the name. The LiteRT-LM, llama.cpp and MLX
backends call it. The Ollama backend does not.

``` python
import importlib, importlib.util
import rishi, rishi.core, urai

test_eq(rishi.Chat is urai.Chat, True)
test_eq(hasattr(rishi.core, 'Chat'), False)
for mod in ('llama', 'mlx', 'remote', 'claude', 'copilot', 'ollama'):
    if mod == 'mlx' and not importlib.util.find_spec('mlx'): continue   # Apple Silicon only
    public = importlib.import_module(f'rishi.{mod}').__all__
    assert 'Chat' not in public and 'UsageStats' not in public
```

``` python
test_eq(split_model_path(None), (None, None))
test_eq(split_model_path('mlx-community/Qwen3-4B-4bit'), ('mlx-community/Qwen3-4B-4bit', None))
test_eq(split_model_path('mlx/mlx-community/Qwen3-4B-4bit'), ('mlx-community/Qwen3-4B-4bit', None))
test_eq(split_model_path('model.gguf'), (None, 'model.gguf'))
test_eq(split_model_path('repo/id', 'given/path.gguf'), ('repo/id', 'given/path.gguf'))
```

## A SafePyRun patch

Urai runs the Python code that a model writes through SafePyRun.
SafePyRun up to version 0.2.6 runs each block of code with separate
global and local namespaces. A function defined in the block cannot see
a module imported in the same block. For example, `import math` followed
by a function that calls `math.sqrt` fails with a `NameError`. rishi
replaces the SafePyRun runner with one that uses a single namespace. The
replacement can be removed when SafePyRun fixes this.

The host’s `__name__` and `__builtins__` survive a block that raises or
fails to parse:

``` python
def _drive(coro):
    try: coro.send(None)
    except StopIteration as e: return e.value

host = {'__name__': 'host', '__builtins__': {}}
for bad in ['raise ValueError', 'def (']: test_fail(lambda: _drive(_rishi_run_python(bad, host)))
test_eq(host['__builtins__'], {})
host['__name__']
```

## Model capabilities

A `Caps` record lists the kinds of input and output a model takes. You
can check it before you send a picture to a model. Urai reads the `Caps`
record of a hosted model from the fastllm model table. Local models have
no such table. Each local runtime supplies a function that inspects the
model.
[`litert_caps`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rishi/core.html#litert_caps)
reports text, image and audio for every LiteRT-LM model. LiteRT-LM
builds the vision and audio encoders whenever multimodal input is on.
[`ollama_caps_`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rishi/core.html#ollama_caps_)
asks the Ollama daemon, which holds the model weights.

## The seven backends

`BACKENDS` holds one `Runtime` record per backend. A record has the
backend name, the class that implements it, a capabilities function, and
the name patterns that identify its models. Urai imports the class when
the backend is first used. When `Chat` gets a model name and no runtime,
Urai tries the patterns in list order and takes the first match. Ollama
comes before llama.cpp in the list. The id `hf.co/unsloth/Qwen3-4B-GGUF`
contains `gguf`, but it is an Ollama id and not a file for llama.cpp.
LiteRT-LM is the default when no model is named.

Claude Code and Copilot have no patterns, because their model names look
like hosted model names. Choose them with a `claude/` or `copilot/`
prefix, or with `runtime='claude'` or `runtime='copilot'`. The tests
below show which names go to which backend. A name that matches no
pattern raises an error.

``` python
test_eq(list(RUNTIMES), ['litert', 'ollama', 'llama', 'mlx', 'remote', 'claude', 'copilot'])
test_eq(infer_runtime('gemma-3n-E4B.litertlm'), 'litert')
test_eq(infer_runtime('hf.co/unsloth/Qwen3-4B-GGUF'), 'ollama')   # asked before llama
test_eq(infer_runtime('qwen3-4b-Q4_K_M.gguf'), 'llama')
test_eq(infer_runtime('mlx-community/Qwen3-4B-4bit'), 'mlx')
test_eq(infer_runtime('gpt-5.1'), 'remote')
```

``` python
test_eq(resolve_runtime('claude-sonnet-4.6'), ('remote', 'claude-sonnet-4.6'))
test_eq(resolve_runtime('claude/claude-sonnet-4.6'), ('claude', 'claude-sonnet-4.6'))
test_eq(resolve_runtime()[0], 'litert')                  # nothing named: the default runtime
test_fail(lambda: resolve_runtime('some-unknown-name'), contains="Can't tell which backend")
```

``` python
test_eq(model_caps('gemma-3n-E4B.litertlm').source, 'runtime')
test_eq({'text', 'image'} - set(model_caps('gpt-5.1').inp), set())   # fastllm's table grows, e.g. 'pdf'
test_eq(resolve('gpt-5.1').local, False)
test_eq(resolve('anything.litertlm').local, True)
```

## Compatibility names

Some functions moved from rishi to Urai and got new names. The old names
remain as aliases. For example, `mk_oai_msg` is an alias of `mk_msg`,
and `browser_approval` is an alias of `http_approval`. Use Urai’s names
in new code, as the rishi backends do.

## Installing the skill

The wheel includes a `skill.md` file that tells a coding agent how to
use rishi.
[`mv_skill_md`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rishi/core.html#mv_skill_md)
copies it to `.agents/skills/rishi/SKILL.md` and
`.claude/skills/rishi/SKILL.md`, where agents look for skills. The
target root is the `dir` argument if you pass one. Otherwise it is the
root of the current git repository, found by
[`repo_root`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rishi/core.html#repo_root).
Outside a repository, the target root is the current folder.
[`repo_root`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rishi/core.html#repo_root)
returns None outside a repository. By default
[`mv_skill_md`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rishi/core.html#mv_skill_md)
prints the target paths and copies nothing. Pass `dry_run=False` to
copy. If
[`mv_skill_md`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rishi/core.html#mv_skill_md)
finds no `skill.md`, it returns without output.
